jurisdiction.name: Mongolia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Mongolia governs AI through its first national strategy, the National Big Data and AI Strategy approved in September 2025, which promises an AI legal framework. AI-relevant clauses already exist in the 2021 personal data law, which requires an assessment of processing done without human involvement and lets people contest automated decisions, and the 2024 law on supporting the IT industry, which sets up an AI sandbox and AI grants. A draft Law on Data that would ban significant decisions made solely by AI and set rules for AI use of data went to public consultation in June 2026 and was sent to parliament in August 2026; there is no AI-specific law yet.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Communications
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft data law is recorded as a consultation draft, and a planned AI law and several implementing procedures are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Их өгөгдөл, хиймэл оюуны үндэсний стратеги
instruments.english_title: National Strategy for Big Data and Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Mongolia (Cabinet), on the proposal of the Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Communications
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Communications
instruments.summary: Mongolia's first national AI strategy, approved by the Government on 24 September 2025 (decision No. 18 per the ministry's policy-document register), with the vision of making Mongolia the digital-economy 'oasis' of Central Asia and one of Asia's top 10 AI countries, implemented in two stages (2025-2027 and 2028-2030). Its four objectives are putting national big data into economic circulation, building an ethical and responsible AI system through public-private cooperation, raising productivity in priority sectors (mining, energy, finance, education, health, agriculture, environment) with privately developed AI, and attracting investment in AI data-centre infrastructure. Measures include drafting a primary data law, creating a national legal framework for AI grounded in human rights, ethics and safety, embedding AI functions in state bodies, AI curricula at all education levels, and indicators such as an AI-ethics readiness score of 4/5 by 2030; the digital-development ministry monitors implementation and reports to the Government at the end of each stage.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; commits to an AI legal framework, the data law and responsible-AI governance in public bodies.
instruments.current_status: Approved 24 September 2025 according to the ministry's register (decision No. 18) and its Q3 2025 implementation report; the 4-page strategy text was published on mddic.gov.mn in February 2026. The Cabinet's English news page for 24 September 2025 describes the draft being discussed and its objectives being integrated into the 2026-2030 Five-Year Development Guidelines. Not yet verified from the official text: the approving decision itself. The ministry declared 2026 the sector's 'Year of Big Data and AI'.

instruments.official_title: Хүний хувийн мэдээлэл хамгаалах тухай хууль
instruments.english_title: Law on Protection of Personal Information
instruments.summary: Mongolia's general personal data protection law (revised edition), adopted 17 December 2021 and applicable from 1 May 2022, governing collection, processing, use and security of personal information by persons, legal entities and public bodies. Article 23 allows controllers to use technology that processes data electronically without human involvement, but requires an assessment, submitted to the National Human Rights Commission for a recommendation, where such processing makes decisions affecting a data subject's rights or regularly processes sensitive data; the assessment methodology is approved by the digital-development ministry on the Commission's proposal. It also treats biometric (including facial) and genetic data as sensitive, restricts their collection to listed purposes, and gives data subjects the right to contest decisions resulting from processing (art. 16.1.11).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated (no-human-involvement) processing and decisions, biometric data and impact assessment that apply to AI systems processing personal data.
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 May 2022 (art. 32.1); legalinfo.mn lists later amendments to the law (16 amendment entries in the portal's amendment list). The National Human Rights Commission of Mongolia gives recommendations on assessments and sensitive-data processing.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full consolidated text read on legalinfo.mn (official legislation portal); adoption 17 Dec 2021 in the header, applicability 1 May 2022 in art. 32.1, automated-processing assessment in art. 23. Status note: The consolidated text was read.

instruments.official_title: Мэдээллийн технологийн үйлдвэрлэлийг дэмжих тухай хууль
instruments.english_title: Law on Supporting the Information Technology Industry
instruments.summary: Law adopted on 5 June 2024 setting state policy, principles and support measures for the information technology industry, including a virtual zone for registered IT companies and financing sources for support. It explicitly tasks the Government with establishing a sandbox based on advanced technologies including artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain and space industry and approving its procedure (art. 6.1.6), and provides grants for AI-based projects where at least 60% of the total cost is self-financed (art. 13.3.4).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with explicit AI provisions: legal basis for an AI/advanced-technology regulatory sandbox and for AI project grants.
instruments.current_status: Adopted 5 June 2024 and listed on legalinfo.mn; the read text gives no separate commencement article, so the effective date is left blank. Not yet verified from the official text: the sandbox procedure required by art. 6.1.6.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text read on legalinfo.mn; date 5 June 2024 in the header; AI sandbox in art. 6.1.6 and AI project grants in art. 13.3.4

instruments.issuing_authority: Legal Research Institute (consultation on legalinfo.mn); draft prepared by the Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Communications
instruments.summary: Draft primary law on data governance, data infrastructure and data-centre activity, published for public comment on legalinfo.mn on 5 June 2026 (comments until 20 June 2026). It would prohibit decisions or profiling affecting a person's or legal entity's legal status, reputation or financial capacity made solely by automated systems or artificial intelligence and require human oversight of automated processing (art. 9.7), set requirements for using data in AI, machine-learning and automated decision systems (lawful source, isolated computing for personal or secret data, secure retention of training data, logs, prompts and inference history, anti-re-identification and anti-profiling controls; art. 10.9), and make system owners and users liable for harm from automated decisions (art. 10.10).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Proposed binding AI/automated-decision rules (ban on solely automated significant decisions, AI data-use requirements, liability).
instruments.current_status: Consultation closed 20 June 2026 (portal status 'comments completed'). The ministry reported in August 2026 that the draft Law on Data had been submitted to Parliament. Not yet verified from the official text: the bill as submitted. Not adopted.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Mongolia's legislation portal, the digital ministry, the Cabinet, other ministries and regulators were searched. Records include the personal information law, the IT industry law, a draft data law and the national big data and AI strategy; there was no material for procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, indices, specific sectors, generative AI, international instruments or older publications. Parliament's own bill search was not used, some ministry sites were checked by web search only, and a ministerial order on automated processing and the AI content of a scanned policy recommendation remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. parliament.mn bill search not queried; legalinfo.mn advanced title search returned empty responses (site-restricted web searches used); education and health ministries web search only. Strategy approval date from the ministry register (Cabinet news describes the draft as discussed). IT-industry law effective date not stated. Digital First Resolution 108 is a scan without text. Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: legalinfo.mn (official legislation portal) read directly: Law on Protection of Personal Information (2021, art. 23 automated processing) and Law on Supporting the IT Industry (2024, AI sandbox and grants) recorded; draft Law on Data (consultation June 2026) recorded. No AI-specific law or AI bill found; parliament.mn not searched by its own engine (portal search via web only). Five-Year Development Guidelines 2026-2030 (Parliament resolution No. 109 of 2025) read: 'Science, technology and AI' is one of eight policy directions but its only target (8.1) is a knowledge-index goal, so not recorded. Forensic e-technology analysis procedure (joint order A/315, A/91 of 13 Sept 2023) lists AI/IoT analysis as one forensic type; judged marginal, not recorded.; Government: Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Communications (mddic.gov.mn) legal-framework register, news and media searched: National Big Data and AI Strategy (approved 24 Sept 2025) recorded; 'Digital First' recommendation (Resolution 108) held as lead (scanned). Cabinet (cabinet.gov.mn) English news page and Cabinet Secretariat 2025 annual report checked (AI use in 11-11 call centre and AI model/server procurement are operational, no governance document). No public-sector AI/GenAI guideline found.; Ministries: Searched (web) education, health, justice: no AI-specific guidance found. Health digital-transformation plan (A/201, A/81 of 2025) and the joint forensic procedure not recorded as AI instruments. Defence, finance/tax, labour, interior: searched, nothing found.; Regulators: Data protection oversight sits with the National Human Rights Commission (no AI guidance or decision found). Bank of Mongolia: searched, nothing AI-specific (only a research brochure). Financial Regulatory Commission: only an ADB-consultant FinTech Innovation Roadmap draft (Mar 2025) with a passing AI mention, not an FRC AI document, not recorded. Communications Regulatory Commission: only a 2024 conference presentation on big data/AI regulation, not a regulatory document. National cyber authority: cyber risk assessment procedure exists but not AI-specific. Standards: no Mongolian adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 found. Convention 108: Mongolia is not a party (not a Council of Europe member; no accession act found).. Not reached: parliament.mn own bill search (not queried directly; draft Law on Data bill page not located); legalinfo.mn advanced title search (POST endpoint returned empty responses; site-restricted web search used instead); mecs.gov.mn / moh.gov.mn own sites (web searches only). Could not verify: Ministerial order A/81 (1 Sept 2023) on assessment of automated processing under PDP law art. 23.3 (only a search snippet; not located on official sites).; AI content of the 'Digital First' policy recommendation (Government Resolution No. 108, 24 Sept 2025) - scanned PDF without text layer.. procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, international, historical: no material found.
